newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Bank of Korea steps in to slow won's fall vs dlr.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Korea steps in to slow won's fall vs dlr.

text.p: The central bank of Korea intervened in the interbank market in early morning trading on Friday to support the falling won against the dollar, dealers said.
The bank denied stepping into the market, as it routinely does.
Dealers said the central bank started selling dollars when the won slipped to 845.00.
They said the market has been short on dollars as demand for the U.S. currency grew on the back of expected import settlements.
Without central bank support, the local unit is forecast to fall again, traders said.
The won is currently trading at 843.00.
